## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The PR adds millisecond timeouts, port validation, configuration loading, and host normalization, and deletes the default configuration. Changes are needed before merge: default loading now fails, port 65535 is rejected, and configuration errors are hidden. Review was static; tests were read but not run.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Deleting this file leaves `app.startup.load_defaults()` reading a nonexistent path — Every call to load the bundled defaults raises `FileNotFoundError`.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns false because the upper bound is exclusive, despite the documented inclusive range — A valid TCP port is rejected.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — `except Exception` silently converts missing files, permission errors, and malformed JSON into `{}` without documenting the fallback — Callers cannot distinguish a failed configuration load from a valid empty configuration or diagnose the underlying error.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring says “returns None when h is empty,” but the empty-input branch executes `return ""` — Callers following the documentation can fail to recognize an empty host when checking for `None`.
- app/parse.py:38 — tests — No test exercises the trailing-dot branch; the only host test uses `"Example.COM"` — A regression leaving `"Example.COM."` as `"example.com."` would pass the current suite.

## Strengths
- The added timeout test checks that `"1500ms"` produces `1.5` seconds.
- The optional JSON accelerator has an explicitly documented standard-library fallback.
